annotations.annotation_text: Page 27 opens Book 1, Chapter 1 ("The Fall of Finnegan") during the Age of Gods (Theocratic) phase. This passage continues the mythic fall of Tim Finnegan / HCE, the thunderclap awakening primitive religion, and the recumbent giant embedded in the Dublin landscape, featuring HCE, Finn MacCool, Mutt and Jute. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Kevin" on page 27 ("The Fall of Finnegan"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within the mythic fall of Tim Finnegan / HCE, the thunderclap awakening primitive religion, and the recumbent giant embedded in the Dublin landscape. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Gods (Theocratic) phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
